<div class="faq"><details class="details alert alert--info details"><summary><h4>Are advanced staggers only useful for grids?</h4></summary><div class="details__inner" style="height: 0px;"><div class="answer"><p>Absolutely not! You can get some slick effects by leveraging <code>ease</code> to add more organic spacing, or use the <code>from</code> property to have things emanate outward from a specific element index or the <code>"center"</code>. Even just using <code>amount</code> can be useful because it gives you tight control over when all the staggering will finish regardless of how many elements are in the target array.</p></div></div></details><details class="details alert alert--info details"><summary><h4>Does <code>grid: "auto"</code> work for responsive layouts after resize?</h4></summary><div class="details__inner" style="height: 0px;"><div class="answer"><p>No, stagger values get calculated immediately when the stagger method is called, so if the layout changes after that, you'd need to handle that logic on your own. For example, you could use a timeline's stagger method so that everything is in one instance, then have a resize listener that rewinds the timeline to its starting values, clears it, and then redoes the stagger. <code>timeline.time(0).clear(); timeline.to(...);</code> Ask in the <a href="https://gsap.com/community/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="">forums</a> if you need any help with that.</p></div></div></details><details class="details alert alert--info details"><summary><h4>What if my elements aren't in a uniform grid (gaps, different sizes, etc.) - can I stagger them based on position?</h4></summary><div class="details__inner" style="height: 0px;"><div class="answer"><p>Sure, that's the perfect time to use a function-based value. In fact, we've created a <a href="https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/gyWrPO?editors=0010" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="">distributeByPosition() helper function</a> for this very case
